source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Bounded models, workshop stories and worked derivations are originally authored constructed examples. No production measurements or historical priority claims are presented.
purpose: Follow changing lengths through their mean and squared deviations into population variance and standard deviation.
meaning: Variance averages squared deviations from a mean. Standard deviation is its nonnegative square root. Equal-scale squared areas expose the distinction between signed length differences, squared spread and spread in the original units.

definition.setting: Population variance and standard deviation for a complete four-length workshop group.

signature.xᵢ: One of the four complete-group measurements.
signature.∑xᵢ: Sum of all four lengths in centimetres.
signature.(x−μ)²: Squared last deviation in square centimetres.
signature.∑(xᵢ−μ)²: Sum of squared deviations in square centimetres.
signature.dᵢ: Signed deviation of measurement i from the current mean, in centimetres.

conditions: The complete group contains four known strip lengths: 8,10,12,x cm, with 0≤x≤20 cm.
Use population variance: divide the four squared deviations by N=4. This is not the sample estimator with denominator N−1.
The mean μ changes with x. Each signed deviation is a length in cm; its square and the variance have units cm².
Standard deviation σ is the nonnegative square root of variance and has units cm. The unequal fixed first three lengths prevent zero variance in this specimen.
The deviation notation is dᵢ=xᵢ−μ for i=1,2,3,4; d₄=x−μ is the changing last strip’s signed deviation.
definition.domain_notes: This is a descriptive calculation for four known values. No confidence interval, uncertainty estimate for an unknown population or sample-variance correction is produced. Zero signed-deviation sum does not imply zero squared spread.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources; restricted-family properties are author-derived. Independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: N=4; μ=(8+10+12+x)/4. Form each signed deviation dᵢ=xᵢ−μ, square it, add the four squares and divide by four: σ²=∑(xᵢ−μ)²/4. Then σ=√(σ²). In this fixed family, σ²=2+(3/16)(x−10)².
grammar.precedence: Compute the current mean before subtracting it; square before adding; take the square root after averaging.

prompts.prompt: Why not average the signed deviations?
prompts.answer: They sum to zero by the arithmetic-mean identity. Squaring prevents opposite signs from cancelling spread.
The four known values are the whole group being described. A sample estimator for an unknown population is a different statistic.
